sources: Saudi-led coalition statement via Reuters (Cairo, Enas Alashray)
fault_line: Did Ansar Allah fire target holy sites / is the debris evidence real? Social comments on the Oct 24 Mecca-debris post split between prayers for Mecca's protection and accusations the story is fabricated for sympathy.

sections.what_happened: The Saudi-led coalition said Tuesday it intercepted and destroyed 3 Ansar Allah ballistic missiles toward Saudi Arabia's Eastern Region and 4 drones toward the Southern Region. Saudi Civil Defense issued early-warning alerts for the Eastern Region and Kharj governorate, later saying the danger had passed in both. Reuters context: Saudi strikes on the Ansar Allah intensified since the group captured strategic Red Sea coast areas last month, advancing toward Bab el-Mandeb; the renewed fighting shattered the 2022 UN-brokered truce. No damage, casualty or Ansar Allah-response detail in the Reuters item. DISTINCT from the Oct 26 '3 drones over Riyadh' item (totw-20261027-0100-01) and the Sunday 10-missile exchange (totw-20261025-1700-01).
sections.what_verified: Reuters reporting of coalition statement; all carries are the same Reuters story
sections.what_disputed: No Ansar Allah claim of this wave retrieved in-window; no independent confirmation of intercepts or of any impact.
sections.why_matters: Fresh wave, counted number: 7 projectiles stopped before dawn -- Eastern Region missiles + Southern drones + Kharj alerts. Pair with the Mecca-debris fault line the audience is already arguing about.
